summary: Observation of two very bright points.
description: An amateur astronomer reports that on November 5, 2005, between 6:41 PM and 6:45 PM, he observed two very bright points located 10 arcseconds east above the horizon. These two white spheres were the size and magnitude of Mars (very visible at this time of year). Their brightness gradually and rapidly diminished until they disappeared completely. The available data is contradictory (stationary phenomena and phenomena moving very quickly, observation duration poorly defined between 30 seconds and 5 minutes) and does not allow for a thorough investigation. The level of strangeness is low (it could be an atmospheric reentry, but the imprecise data on the duration do not allow for confirmation). No element on the sky chart allows for the identification of this phenomenon, which is classified as Class C.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena in the night sky: probable astronomical observations.
description: On November 1, 2005, between 6:25 PM and 6:45 PM, witnesses observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon in the sky: a very bright white ball with two red dots on either side. This phenomenon moved very slowly and silently toward the southwest without changing direction. The same observation was made two weeks later by the same person. The local gendarmerie brigade noted the presence of a star. The witness, during their first observation, was likely also making an astronomical observation. Examination of the star chart at the time of the observation shows a conjunction of Venus, Mercury, Uranus, and Antares, with Venus particularly bright (magnitude -3). It is therefore very likely that the witness observed this group of planets and stars, which was beginning to shine in the setting sun. GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable astronomical observations.

summary: Observation of a light accompanied by a muffled noise.
description: On October 13, 2005, a witness observed a bright light accompanied by a loud noise. No further information was available regarding this sighting. Confusion with a motorized vehicle is likely, but this could not be verified.

summary: Observation of the movement of a boomerang-shaped object.
description: On October 4, 2005, GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Special Operations Group) was alerted by a gendarme at Blagnac Airport who had seen a curious phenomenon moving at the end of a runway. The witness described an object shaped like a boomerang and suspected it was a remote-controlled device, but it disappeared at a significant speed, which surprised the witness. No other witness statements were collected regarding this phenomenon. Reading the report gives a strong impression of credibility: the observation is carefully described in precise and objective terms; the witness's professionalism is evident. The reported facts present a moderate degree of strangeness: although this craft would not have been in the area, its performance remains consistent with that of a remote-controlled device (albeit a high-performance one). The pendulum-like movement observed at the beginning of the observation may have been against the wind, while the rapid movement was with the wind. The description is reminiscent of certain drene models, very rare at that time. However, as the account is old, it is not possible to verify this hypothesis. The classification "C" is assigned to this case, with the "drene" hypothesis insufficiently substantiated.

summary: An aircraft crossed paths with a grey object not recognized by the captain.
description: On July 7, 2005, at 2:14 PM UTC, the captain of Air France flight AF 7705, on approach to Charles de Gaulle Airport, reported that his aircraft crossed paths at less than half a nautical mile with a gray object that appeared to be stationary. The object did not resemble a weather balloon at all. This encounter (reported by an Airprox pilot) between a commercial airliner and a flying object was unusual. The observed shape did not correspond to a balloon, whether scientific, recreational, or festive. No radar echo was detected. The local analysis conducted on the ground by air traffic control found no explanation. It is unclear whether other pilots saw this object. The hypothesis that it was a balloon that had escaped from Disneyland Paris does not initially seem to fit the shape or color: balloons are almost always convex, and Disneyland Paris balloons are typically brightly colored. As it is no longer possible to make progress on this investigation (search for other observations, investigation at Eurodisney) this case is classified as C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the transformation of a boomerang-shaped form.
description: During the night of June 27-28, 2005, at approximately 4:15 a.m., a witness observed the slow passage of a dark, boomerang-like shape with no apparent light or flames, and completely silent. The observation lasted about 8 to 10 seconds. Five to ten minutes later, the witness reported the appearance of fog and a fairly strong breeze. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected. While confusion with an aircraft cannot be ruled out, no other hypothesis could be confirmed due to a lack of information.

On September 29, 2005, a witness provided the police with sunset photographs taken on June 23, 2005, on a beach on the island of Noirmoutier. One of the photographs shows a luminous phenomenon. The photographs were taken along a northwest axis. The witness provided no description of the phenomenon. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observing the evolution of an object
description: On June 19, 2005, a witness observed the movements of an object the size of a small airplane. Very little information is available about this case, but the hypothesis of a small aircraft being observed cannot be ruled out.

On June 13, 2005, at approximately 4:35 PM, a teacher and his students observed a bright point in the sky, about the size of a star. After a few minutes, this point appeared to split in two, and in the following minutes, the witness observed several points moving slowly relative to one another, resembling airliners at very high altitude. The witness took photographs with his cell phone but did not provide them to the police. The prevailing hypothesis is that the phenomenon was indeed the reflection of the sun on airliners flying at high altitude.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a long, dark-colored shape.
description: An old sighting from 2005, reported in 2010. A possible aircraft was seen in one of the flight paths of Rennes/St Jacques airport, but due to the age of the sighting, any verification of a potential flight or any investigation is impossible. The case is classified as Class C due to lack of information.

On February 18, 2005, at approximately 10:30 PM, two witnesses in two departments in eastern France observed the very rapid passage of a green or white trail, depending on the account, which disappeared within seconds. These individuals likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry. Furthermore, a few days later, the press reported that numerous people in northeastern France had observed a small meteorite fall.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry
description: On February 18, 2005 at approximately 10:20 PM, the crew of a Boeing 737 observed the very brief passage of an extremely bright light on a downward trajectory, identified as a probable atmospheric reentry.

On January 17th at approximately 10:45 PM, a witness on his balcony observed a large, bright object resembling a glider, with a light that appeared red and a faint engine noise. It is likely the witness saw an aircraft.

summary: Passing over a village of two superimposed luminous circles.
description: On January 10, 2005, at approximately 11:00 PM, a witness reported to the BRIA (Brigade de Répression des Infractions Indépendants - Independent Research Brigade) at Marseille airport the passage of two superimposed luminous circles over the village. No further information is available.

summary: Very rapid passage of a point of light in front of a window.
description: In 2005 (the witness doesn't remember the exact date), around 10 PM, a student was about to close his skylight when he was surprised to see a bright object flash across the clear sky at high speed. Its trajectory was northwest-southeast. Spherical in shape and slightly yellowish, this object appeared to be at an altitude of 3,000 meters; no sound was heard. It seemed to be enveloped in a halo. The observation lasted less than three seconds. The description of the object suggests a possible atmospheric reentry, but we lack information about the observed phenomenon.
